items.summary: Governor Rajendra Arlekar has assented to an amendment that lowers the minimum land required to establish a private university in Tamil Nadu from 100 acres across the state to location-based thresholds of as little as 12 acres. The Bill, which amends the Tamil Nadu Private Universities Act, 2019 and was passed by the Legislative Assembly in September 2026, replaces the uniform requirement with three tiers: at least 12 acres within Chennai city limits, 18 acres in other municipal corporations and municipal council areas, and 25 acres elsewhere. The new minimum outside municipal areas is a quarter of the previous threshold.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Governor clears lower land thresholds for private universities

visual.alt: Bar chart. university 100 acre; city limits will require 12 acre; minimum 18 acre; rest of the state 25 acre.

items.summary: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik was permitted to visit the Taj Mahal in Agra during his trip to India but denied entry to the Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah in Delhi on security grounds. The Ministry of External Affairs announced these decisions Saturday (November 21) via news agency ANI, and Malik's delegation had also been cleared for other Delhi sites including Humayun's Tomb and Dilli Haat while his request for the dargah was turned down by both security agencies and the MEA. Malik is in India from November 20 to 22 to attend the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, marking the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in three years; he expressed hope that engagement between the two countries would continue and called for broader views on political and social issues to strengthen regional ties. The forum was inaugurated Friday evening at Purana Qila in New Delhi, with all 10 SCO member states plus observer countries and dialogue partners invited.
items.title: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Cleared for Taj Mahal, Denied Nizamuddin Dargah

items.summary: A Delhi fast-track court formally framed charges against all [q2: 14 accused] on Saturday, November 21, in the NEET-UG [d1: 2026] paper leak case. The proceedings took place before Special Judge Ajay Gupta at Rouse Avenue Courts, where the accused pleaded not guilty and opted to face trial over the alleged conspiracy that led to the cancellation of the medical entrance examination in May. Separately, the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) demanded a ban on Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana film 'Rise of a Legend,' with general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra and International President Alok Kumar alleging that demon king Ravana was glorified and facts distorted.
items.title: Delhi Court Frames Charges Against 14 in NEET-UG Paper Leak Case; VHP Objects to Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana

items.summary: Justice BV Nagarathna, who is expected to become India's first woman Chief Justice in September 2027, argued at the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College, University of Oxford, that the presence of a few distinguished women in high public office does not reflect gender equality across society. She called for deeper examination of structural barriers limiting women's access to education, employment and professional advancement, warning against measuring progress merely by counting discriminatory laws struck down or beneficial statutes enacted. Justice Nagarathna urged one-third representation for women lawyers on government panels representing the State and providing legal aid, drawing a parallel with constitutional amendments reserving seats for women in panchayats, municipalities, Parliament and state legislatures. Her remarks come against persistent gender imbalance in India's higher judiciary: the Supreme Court has three women among its 37 sitting judges, while women account for only 111 of the 781 sitting judges across the country's 25 high courts, or around 14%. She traced the evolution of women's rights from colonial law to constitutional equality under Articles 14 and 21, citing landmark judgments including the 2005 recognition of daughters as equal coparceners in ancestral property, Vishaka guidelines against workplace harassment, Anuj Garg rejecting protective paternalism restricting women's opportunities, and her own ruling on a Sikkimese tax exemption that struck down discrimination based on marital status. She cautioned that equality must account for intersecting disadvantages from caste, class, disability, religion, region and economic circumstances, noting the disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work shapes women's choices.
items.title: Supreme Court judge BV Nagarathna: Women in high office does not mean equality has been achieved

items.summary: The Pentagon released 43 files on Friday, including a 538-page report by government contractor Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) dated July 2009. The report outlined plans for a highly secure underground vault in North Las Vegas, Nevada, buried 15 to 20 feet deep with three-foot-thick walls and extensive camouflage, featuring a storage area spanning 5,000 square feet intended to hold potentially recovered 'exotic material or tissue,' biological samples, and unidentified hardware. However, the document described only proposed plans and anticipated acquisitions; it does not establish that BAASS had actually recovered extraterrestrial material or that the vault was ever built. The files also contain accounts of UFO sightings dating back to 1953 involving Lockheed engineer Clarence 'Kelly' Johnson, who reportedly observed a dark elliptical object hovering for about three minutes before an Air Force assessment classified it as a lenticular cloud; a December 1956 encounter near Ube, Japan in which a fighter pilot detected an unidentified radar return lasting seven to eight minutes and estimated the object moving at 1,500 to 1,800 knots without ground or wingman confirmation. More recent encounters include the 2004 USS Nimitz incident, a 2007 encounter near RAF Lakenheath in Britain, and three videos captured by US Central Command in 2020, 2023, and 2026 showing unidentified objects or areas of contrast recorded by military sensors. Despite these unusual accounts, the documents do not establish that any sightings involved extraterrestrial objects or technology.
items.title: Pentagon Releases UFO Files Detailing Proposed Nevada Vault for 'Exotic' Material and Decades of Unexplained Sightings

items.summary: The Odisha Janata Congress (OJC) announced a gherao of the state Legislative Assembly on November 23 to protest what it called spiralling prices of essential commodities and alleged BJP government inaction. Party chief Mohammed Moquim said around 5,000 party workers would take part, targeting middle-class, lower-middle-class and economically weaker households whose incomes he said had failed to keep pace with rising household expenditure. He cited onions at Rs 70 per kg and LPG cylinders reaching around Rs 1,000 amid reduced Ujjwala subsidy availability, along with higher electricity bills over the past two-and-a-half years, unfulfilled promises on price control, VAT reduction on petrol and diesel, and cold storage facilities in every block. OJC media cell chairman Prashant Satpathy claimed Odisha had become the fifth most expensive state nationally, with retail inflation at 7.17 per cent above the national average, blaming fuel, electricity costs and food prices; he also criticised the State government's silence on the cost-of-living crisis. General secretary Shubhendhu Mallik said office-bearers across levels plus student, youth and women's wing leaders would join the protest to force concrete anti-inflation measures and consumer relief.
items.title: Odisha Janata Congress Plans Assembly Gherao Over Rising Prices and Inflation
